---
title: "How long should it fly for?"
---


::: {#5269907f .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
plane, layout = glider()
res = glide(plane, layout)

h_total = launch_height()
h_zoom = h_total - H_RELEASE
h_sweep = np.linspace(0, 6, 61)

s_per_m = 1.0 / res["sink"]

# Every number on this page is an inline expression reading this dict, so the
# page tracks the model rather than the day it was written. These guard the two
# claims the PROSE makes that are not themselves quoted numbers: that the zoom
# is the larger contribution, and that the seconds-per-metre figure is close
# enough to unity to be described as roughly one.
assert h_zoom > H_RELEASE
assert 0.8 < s_per_m < 1.25
```
:::


::: {.hero}
[3\.0 s]{.hero-value}
[time aloft, from a gentle toss, in still air]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** It sinks at 1\.09 m/s, so every metre of
launch height buys [0\.92 s]{.key} aloft (@fig-duration).
The toss supplies 3\.3 m —
1\.5 m from the hand and
1\.8 m from the zoom — and the glide spends it at L/D
[4\.4]{.key}, flying at
4\.9 m/s.

::: {.callout-warning}
## This is the floor, not the target
Nothing is optimised yet, and the arm supplies
46% of the height.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Specified

Asked of the user, 2026-09-03:

1. **Launch: 8 m/s**, a gentle level toss.
2. **Release height: 1\.5 m** — thrown from the shoulder.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumed

1. **Zoom efficiency: 55%** of launch energy becomes height.
2. **Static margin: 30%**, the tightest that trims.
3. **Still air** — no thermal, no gust, no lift.
:::

::: {#cell-fig-duration .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(h_sweep, h_sweep / res["sink"], label="glide from height $h$")
ax.axvline(H_RELEASE, ls="--", color="C2", lw=1.2, label="release height")
ax.plot(h_total, res["duration"], "o", color="C1", ms=7, label="specified toss")
ax.set_xlabel("launch height, m")
ax.set_ylabel("time aloft, s")
ax.set_xlim(0, 6)
ax.set_ylim(0, None)
ax.grid()
ax.legend()
plt.show()
```
